**On the academic job market, 2026–27 · Defending May 2027**\
Fields: World Politics, Quantitative Methodology

I am a political scientist studying violence and rhetoric using computational methods and causal inference. I ask why political outsiders — insurgents, revolutionaries, and activists — speak differently from politicians.

My dissertation, *The Language of Non-Institutional Politics and Power*, shows that outsiders rely on an action-oriented rhetoric and that a movement organization's power explains its intensity. I test the argument on one of the largest original corpora on non-institutional politics to date: roughly one million pages of movement periodicals and legislative speech, with external validation from interwar U.S. data.

## Selected credentials

- Best Paper Award, *International Interactions* (2021)

## Interests

Outsider Politics & Mobilization · Political Violence & Conflict · Text-as-Data & NLP · Causal Inference

## Methods training

*University of Michigan; ICPSR*

**Text-as-Data & NLP.** POS tagging, dependency parsing, topic modeling, word embeddings, transformer models, dictionary methods, OCR and web scraping

**Statistics & Causal Inference.** Synthetic control, instrumental variables, difference-in-differences, matching, directed acyclic graphs

**Additional.** Spatial analysis and GIS, network theory, game theory

**Software.** R, Stata, LaTeX, ArcGIS
